narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic journey and determined that there’s an **80% chance** you may not pass your final year. This is a strong signal that, without support, you could face serious challenges in completing your studies. Because of this high risk, you’ve been required to take remedial courses to help you catch up and improve your chances of success.

The decision isn’t random—it’s based on three key factors that stood out in your situation. The most important was your **history of past academic struggles**, which is far more common among students who don’t finish their final year. Unlike most students who’ve never failed a class, you’ve had at least one failure before, making it harder to recover lost time and confidence.

Another major influence was your **mother’s level of education**. While many students have parents with higher education, yours completed only primary school. Research shows that when parents have less formal education, students often face additional challenges in accessing resources, encouragement, or even understanding how to navigate school expectations. This doesn’t mean your mother isn’t supportive—she is—but it highlights an area where extra guidance could make a big difference.

The third factor, surprisingly, worked *in your favor*: your clear goal to pursue higher education. Most students in your situation also want to continue their studies, so this actually reduced the model’s concern slightly. However, it wasn’t enough to outweigh the other risks.

To move forward, focus on the areas where you can take control. Your remedial courses are designed to address your past academic gaps, so treat them as a chance to rebuild your confidence. Since you’re already receiving family support, lean on that network while also seeking extra help—whether through tutoring, study groups, or school resources. Small, consistent efforts, like reducing absences and managing your time better, can shift the odds in your favor. This isn’t about failure—it’s about recognizing where you need support and using it to turn things around.
